sourcedFrom: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") (undated beyond "V26.1" on the back page)
cleanIntro:
The PWS BDE22-Ti is a 3D-printed titanium rimfire can with a DLC-coated exterior, rated up to 5.7x28mm and for full-auto and rapid fire. It threads straight onto a 1/2-28 muzzle. It is built to come apart: inside the tube is a single monocore, threaded to an entrance chamber at the back, and an end cap closes the front. Its taper threads are there to fight carbon locking.

The routine never opens the can: it comes off the host, you look through the bore, clean the outside with a nylon brush and CLP, and check that everything is tight. Deep Clean is PWS's own disassembly with the supplied wrench: end cap off, tube off, monocore out and off its entrance chamber, every part brushed or soaked in CLP. PWS recommends cleaning, lubricating and checking torque every 500 rounds.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, host cleared by its own manual
steps.action: Point the host's muzzle in a safe direction and keep it there. Clear the host firearm by its own manual before your hands go near the can: this book teaches the suppressor and prints no clearing procedure for any host.
steps.prose: Your hand is about to be wrapped around the muzzle end. Treat the gun as loaded until you have seen it empty.
steps.quote: ALWAYS KEEP THE MUZZLE OF A FIREARM POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION REGARDLESS OF WHETHER THE FIREARM IS LOADED.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Warnings, item 1, p.6
steps.warn: TREAT ALL FIREARMS AS LOADED AT ALL TIMES.

steps.title: Rated up to 5.7x28mm
steps.action: Before going further, check what this can has been fed. PWS rates the BDE 22 up to 5.7x28mm, and for full-auto and rapid fire. Nothing bigger goes through it.
steps.prose: PWS warns that the wrong ammunition can jam, fail to fire or build excessive pressure.
steps.quote: THE BDE® 22 IS RATED UP TO 5.7x28MM AND FULL AUTO / RAPID FIRE
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Specifications, p.8

steps.title: Let it cool before you touch it
steps.action: Do not handle the can hot. Let the firearm and the suppressor cool completely before you touch either, and set it down where it touches nothing while it cools.
steps.prose: PWS: a suppressor gets far hotter than the 140°F skin-burn limit, and a hot can does not look hot.
steps.caution: Suppressor can cause burn, damage, or destroy anything it touches; ensure your suppressor is not in contact with anything while it cools.
steps.quote: Do not handle a hot suppressor. Allow the firearm and suppressor to completely cool prior to any contact.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Warnings, Suppressors Get Hot, p.4

steps.title: Can off the host's 1/2-28 threads
steps.action: Unscrew the can from the host's 1/2-28 muzzle threads by hand. PWS's book prints no removal procedure for the host. If it is carbon-locked to the muzzle, do not force it.
steps.prose: Note how tight it was when it came off: it tells you whether it was staying put.
steps.quote: UNIVERSAL 1/2-28 TPI PATTERN FOR COMPATIBILITY WITH MOST .22 CALIBER FIREARMS.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Why BDE, Compatible, p.9

steps.title: Look through the bore
steps.action: Look through the can from end to end for anything blocking the bore, including mud or sand.
steps.prose: An obstruction in the bore of a suppressor is something a bullet will find.
steps.quote: Visually inspect the suppressor for any bore obstructions including natural matter like mud and/or sand.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Maintenance, p.12

steps.title: Nylon brush and CLP on the outside
steps.action: Clean the outside of the can with a nylon brush and a CLP-type product. The exterior is DLC coated, so some cleaners and solvents must not be used on it. Wear gloves and safety goggles, and work in a well-ventilated place away from open flame.
steps.prose: PWS warns that cleaning a suppressor carries potential toxicity.
steps.caution: Please be aware that the exterior is DLC (Diamond-like carbon) coated, so certain cleaners and solvents should not be used.
steps.quote: To clean any part of this assembly, use a nylon brush with CLP (Cleaner, Lubricant, Preservative) type of product.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Maintenance, p.12
steps.warn: When cleaning a suppressor, you should wear gloves and safety goggles.

steps.title: Every part tight
steps.action: Check that every part of the can is tight. If the tube turns, the end cap needs tightening more: when it is tight the tube does not spin.
steps.prose: PWS ties this to accuracy: a loose part is a can out of line.
steps.aside: Note: If tube is loose, tighten end cap more. When tight the tube should not spin.
steps.quote: Regular tightening should be done on all parts of the suppressor to ensure accuracy is maintained.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Maintenance, p.12

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The can is off the host, cool, its bore inspected, its outside clean and every part checked tight. That is the routine. Deep Clean is PWS's own disassembly: the supplied wrench, end cap off, tube off, monocore out, every part cleaned.
steps.prose: PWS recommends cleaning, lubricating and checking torque every 500 rounds.
steps.quote: Your PWS BDE® Suppressor should be routinely checked and maintained for preventative measures.
steps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Maintenance, p.12

deepSteps.title: The supplied wrench separates every part
deepSteps.action: Take the wrench that came with the can. PWS's disassembly uses it to separate each part of the assembly.
deepSteps.prose: Four parts come apart: end cap, outer tube, monocore (the baffle stack) and entrance chamber.
deepSteps.quote: To disassemble the BDE® 22, simply use the supplied wrench to separate each part of the assembly.
deepSteps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: End cap loose, tube off the baffle stack
deepSteps.action: Loosen the end cap first. Then turn the tube and take it off the baffle stack.
deepSteps.prose: End cap first, then the tube.
deepSteps.quote: First, loosen the end cap, turn and remove the tube from the baffle stack.
deepSteps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Carbon-locked parts: the wrench, not force
deepSteps.action: If a part will not turn, use the wrench to loosen it. Carbon often locks the parts together.
deepSteps.prose: PWS's taper threads help, and regular cleaning is what keeps carbon from locking them.
deepSteps.quote: Use this tool to loosen parts when cleaning. Often, carbon can cause parts to lock up.
deepSteps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Disassembly, p.10

deepSteps.title: Monocore out of the tube, off its entrance chamber
deepSteps.action: Slide the monocore out of the tube. It is threaded to the entrance chamber at the back; separate the two with the wrench.
deepSteps.prose: Reassembly threads the core back onto the entrance chamber, so this is the joint to undo.
deepSteps.quote: SIMPLY REMOVE ENDCAPS AND SLIDE MONOCORE OUT OF TUBE FOR EASY CLEANING.
deepSteps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Why BDE, Easily Serviceable, p.9

deepSteps.title: The monocore stays whole — PWS's stopping point
deepSteps.action: Stop here. On the bench: end cap, outer tube, monocore and entrance chamber. The monocore is one piece and is not taken apart, adjusted or changed.
deepSteps.prose: PWS's disassembly ends at these four parts.
deepSteps.quote: NEVER MANIPULATE, ADJUST, OR CHANGE ANY OF THE INTERNAL COMPONENTS OF YOUR FIREARM AND/OR SUPPRESSOR.
deepSteps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Warnings, item 10, p.6

deepSteps.title: Nylon brush and CLP on every part
deepSteps.action: Clean each part with a nylon brush and a CLP-type product. Keep cleaners and solvents that are not safe on DLC away from the outside of the tube. Gloves and safety goggles, in a well-ventilated place away from open flame.
deepSteps.caution: Please be aware that the exterior is DLC (Diamond-like carbon) coated, so certain cleaners and solvents should not be used.
deepSteps.quote: To clean any part of this assembly, use a nylon brush with CLP (Cleaner, Lubricant, Preservative) type of product.
deepSteps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Maintenance, p.12
deepSteps.warn: When cleaning a suppressor, you should wear gloves and safety goggles.

deepSteps.title: Soak for stuck-on carbon
deepSteps.action: Carbon that the brush will not shift: soak the individual parts in CLP, then brush again.
deepSteps.prose: Soak the parts, not the whole can.
deepSteps.quote: You can soak individual parts in CLP for any stuck-on carbon.
deepSteps.cite: Primary Weapons Systems BDE22-TI Suppressor — Owners Manual — V26.1 — printed on the back page ("BDE22-TI OWNERS MANUAL | V26.1") — Maintenance, p.12

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & BORE
tasks: Interval: clean, lubricate and check torque every 500 rounds
Look through the bore for obstructions, mud and sand included
Nylon brush and CLP on the outside
⚠ The exterior is DLC coated: some cleaners and solvents must not be used on it
Gloves and safety goggles, well-ventilated, away from open flame

cleaning.name: THREADS & TIGHTNESS
tasks: Every part of the can tight
Tube must not spin: if it does, tighten the end cap more
Oil or grease on the threads before it goes back on

cleaning.name: DEEP CLEAN: CORE, TUBE, CAPS
tasks: Deep clean: nylon brush and CLP on the monocore, tube, end cap and entrance chamber
Deep clean: soak individual parts in CLP for stuck-on carbon
Do not manipulate, adjust or change the internal components: the monocore stays whole

reassembly: Oil or grease on the threads of every part, to stop carbon locking them together.
Thread the core onto the entrance chamber and hand tighten it.
Insert the core assembly into the tube.
Screw the end cap onto the assembly and hand tighten it. If the tube is loose, tighten the end cap more: when it is tight the tube does not spin.
Thread the can back onto the host's 1/2-28 muzzle threads, threads oiled or greased, and check that it is tight and fits properly.
Every 500 rounds PWS also wants the torque checked against its 7 ft. lb. figure; the book does not say which joint the figure is for.
fncheck: PWS's book publishes no function check. With the host unloaded and cleared, look through the bore with the can mounted: nothing may block the bullet's path. Check that the can is tight on the host and the tube does not spin. PWS puts checking fit and retention on the owner before every use; if the can is worn, loose or ill-fitting to the host, stop using it.
